title: Structural tuple type
body:
This is to let a core return several results at once with each potentially in a different representation. New operator`(tuple e ...)` constructs a tuple, and `(ref t i)` with an index reads a slot of tuple `t`.

This benchmark goes from ~92% to ~98% accuracy: https://github.com/herbie-fp/herbie/blob/798041284f3e9dcfe261c5965c95dfe2f5f3ba42/bench/tuples/basic.fpcore#L22-L27

Tuple impls are created at first use. For example lowering `(tuple e ...)` builds the constructor `tuple<binary32:binary64>` and per-index accessors `ref.0.tuple<...>` on the fly: https://github.com/herbie-fp/herbie/blob/798041284f3e9dcfe261c5965c95dfe2f5f3ba42/src/syntax/sugar.rkt#L259-L264

A missing impl is rebuilt from its name: `impl-info` synthesizes and retries on lookup miss: https://github.com/herbie-fp/herbie/blob/798041284f3e9dcfe261c5965c95dfe2f5f3ba42/src/syntax/platform.rkt#L203-L216

`impl-exists?` only parses and validates the name
